main_text.l: Vanus adeò & impotens mundi hic est insultus, quum gloriam Dei super nos requiescentem, in ignominiam nobis convertere conatur, ut cœcitate sua, magis misericordiam, quam pravitate indignationem mereatur. Toleremus paululum illorum insaniam, brevi pharmaco divinæ sapientiæ ad meliorem mentem adducti, grato animo amplectentur, quos tanquam insidiatores abominabantur. Tulit hoc Dominus, tulerunt hoc ante nos, majores & meliores nobis Prophetæ & Apostoli, qualisque illorum exitus, obturato adversariorum ore fuerit, præconium ipso-rum toto mundo clarum loquitur. Christus Dominus gloriæ, pro dæmoniaco habitus est; Paulo garrulitas, novarum fabularum venditatio, seditio, delirium objectum fuit: ebrietatem sibi Apostoli, omnes hæresin Christiani, attribui audierunt; ideoque beati erant, nam dixit Christus, quum convitiati fuetint vobis, & vos persecuti fuerint, & dixerint quidvis mali adversus vos, gaudete & exultate, quoniam merces vestra multa est in cælis: ita enim persecuti fuerunt Prophetas, qui ante vos fuerunt. Contemptus sis, peripsc[?]ma sis, abominatio sis infidelibus necesse est; per carnis infirmitatem tibi prædicandū erit

page.notes: The first word "Vanus" and the page's opening are a continuation of the previous page's sentence; cont="true" is used. Line end "ipso-rum" and "con-vertere" are hyphenated at line ends in print. "peripsc[?]ma" is a doubtful Greek-derived word (perhaps periscema / peripsema) and was read with uncertainty. "fuetint" appears to be a printing error for "fuerint" and is left as printed. "Chriftus" and "fi"/"fe" forms are printed with long s and are written with plain s. The catchword "erit," is at the right foot.
